methods.label: Track the radius of each rotation
methods.explanation:
During a rotation, a point follows a circular arc whose radius is its distance from the rotation center. Each \(90^\circ\) turn traces one quarter of a circle.

For the first rotation, the radius is the rectangle's diagonal \(PR\). By the Pythagorean theorem,
\[
PR=\sqrt{2^2+6^2}=2\sqrt{10}.
\]
Therefore, the first part of the path has length
\[
\frac14(2\pi\cdot2\sqrt{10})=\pi\sqrt{10}.
\]
Let \(P_1\) and \(S_1\) be the positions of \(P\) and \(S\) after this rotation. The second rotation is about \(S_1\), so its radius is \(P_1S_1\). Rotation preserves distances, giving \(P_1S_1=PS=6\). The second arc consequently has length \(\frac14(2\pi\cdot6)=3\pi\).

Adding the distances traveled during the two turns gives \(\boxed{(3+\sqrt{10})\pi}\), choice \(\text{C}\).
